text.brief: In August 1950 federal agents in Los Angeles seized the crates of notes that Qian Xuesen, a founder of the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, had packed for a trip home.
text.record: The government had revoked Qian's clearance that June on suspicion of Communist Party ties, a charge he denied ([Caltech Library exhibit: Remembering JPL co-founder Tsien](https://library.caltech.edu/c.php?g=1245983&p=9125566)). Officials held him under restrictions close to house arrest for five years and let him sail for the mainland in September 1955, in a trade tied to the release of American prisoners ([Caltech Aerospace: Qian Xuesen (Tsien Hsue-Shen)](https://aerospace.caltech.edu/about/legends-of-galcit/qian-xuesen-tsien-hsue-shen)). Qian went on to lead the People's Republic's missile program.
text.reading: The United States deported the scientist it had trained on a charge it never proved, and it handed the Party a founder of its missile program. Suspicion by association rather than conduct cost more than any theft.
text.gapText: Architecture Principles. The defender judged a scientist by association and gave the adversary the talent it feared losing.
text.fix: Judge researchers on documented conduct and keep them, because a talent expelled on suspicion becomes the adversary's gain.
